description:

NOTE FROM ANNIE'S MOM - We did NOT disable comments. YouTube did. In their recent cleaning up YouTube kids department they are demonetizing perfectly clean, decent video content, like this video. title: I Wasted 2-Years Of My Life?
description:
Did I just waste 2-years of my life? 

These past two years were nothing like I expected. In this video, I’m sharing what my mission was really like, the good, the hard, and everything in between.

It started with submitting my papers, getting my call, and feeling totally overwhelmed. I had anxiety for the first time in my life, and saying goodbye to my family and girlfriend was way harder than I thought it’d be. Then I was off to Brazil, still in shock, trying to process everything, and stepping into a completely different world.

I started to adjust, and then out of nowhere, I had to get emergency gallbladder surgery and fly back home. That completely threw me off. I didn’t know if I was supposed to go back or if that was it. A while later, I got reassigned to Boston, packed up again, and said goodbye for the second time.

Boston was a whole different experience. In the video, I talk about what my daily life looked like, the people I met, the crazy moments, and the miracles I got to see. I made some of my closest friends, learned how to serve in ways I didn’t expect, and had a lot of time to reflect.

Coming home now, it’s been weird looking back at it all. There were a lot of ups and downs. Moments where I didn’t feel like I was enough, and others where things just clicked. Two years is a long time, and honestly, I’ve been asking myself the same question you saw in the title. So here’s my story, you decide what it all meant. ;)

title: THIS ONE MOMENT CHANGED THE NEXT 5 YEARS OF OUR LIVES..
description:
This one moment in time, changed the course of our lives for the next 5 years..

With our soon to be return to these beautiful lands with some friends this summer we thought this would be the perfect Monday Memories. This time from the very first time we ever discovered Van Life! Our first ever road trip back in 2020 to Scotland. One that left lifetime impressions on all of us! Funny story: We had spend the new year period this year in Edinburgh in an Airbnb. On that trip we met a couple of subscribers that follow this channel who told us all about the incredible road trip called the North Coast 500 or NC500. We had never heard of this but they sold it so well to us that we decided then and there we would do it at some point that year. Then 2020 happened and those plans had to be postponed. But the second we could all move again in the July that year we rented a motorhome (our first ever) and we left for the Highlands! A road trip that still to this day we all talk about, being one of our best ever! Not to mention the start of our obsession with van life and traveling by road. The last 5 years of our lives might have been very different had we not have bumped into those subscribers on that day in Edinburgh. Theres no other place like the Highlands of Scotland. You need to visit it and experience it to know but needless to say, we are very much looking forward to seeing even more of it this summer!

Today I got us Chipotle and I forgot to get Keren guacamole. If you know Keren, she is a very picky eater and has very bad Hrage. Yes you read that right. The H is silent and stands for Hungry rage. If she doesn't get food in her mouth when she is hungry, she automatically turns into the slapping beast aka Keren. So I sat down at the living room table and opened the bag. I realized I had forgotten the guac so I was going to quickly go back to Chipotle and come back. It was too late. Keren walked in and said OOH I'm staaaaarving. I sat down on the couch sweating bullets. She opened the bag and raised an eye brow. At this point, I was so drenched in sweat it looked like I went swimming in our perfectly balanced pH leveled pool. Again, her eye brow raised higher it looked like it was about to bounce off her forehead. She looked at me, her eyes as red as Rudolph the reindeers nose. "WHERE IS MY CHIPOTLE" she growled. "I forgot" I mumbled but before I could finish she smacked me so hard I landed back at Chipotle behind the counter scooping up a soufflé of guacamole. I cried and my salty tears landed in the guac. I brought it back to Keren and she said it tasted delicious. I cried. The guacamole cried with me.  I don't forget guac anymore.

title: WE FOSTERED A CAT
description:
We pulled off the ultimate 3-Hour Surprise Mission! After Sabre and Sockie moved out, the family has been feeling sad. So, Biggy and Naz went on a secret mission, while Papa and the girls were arranging the ultimate surprise: a foster cat named Buttons!

THE SURPRISE: Biggy and Naz had no idea what was happening. We recorded the moment they met Buttons—and their reaction was pure emotion!

FOSTER TO FAIL? We are only fostering Buttons for a week, but the whole family is falling in love with her. What are the chances we end up keeping her forever?

THE DRAMA: We had to clean the whole house for the inspection, survive a near-betrayal from Mom, and narrowly avoid getting the surprise ruined!

PET ADOPTION: We partner with Animaid https://animaid.au/ to show you how easy and straightforward the cat fostering process is.

Watch the whole video to see Biggy and Naz's reactions, and find out if we commit to the ultimate foster fail!

title: ROAD TRIP Across AMERICA… FOOD Challenge! 🍔
description:
We travelled across the US and did a New FOOD CHALLENGE in EVERY STATE! We tried some of the BEST and GROSSEST foods across the US, who do you think wins, Parents or TEENS?   Watch this: https://youtu.be/pr6ZmLHpN30?si=yOUqB7ZRrkDotnYU
Subscribe: https://goo.gl/dRpa1N

**IN TODAYS VIDEO: We share...
*Togetherness Over Winning
“It’s not about who wins — it’s about doing it together.” The best adventures aren’t about victory — they’re about shared memories and laughter through the mess.
*Embracing the Journey (Not Just the Destination)
“Every state had something crazy… but that’s what made it unforgettable.”
Each stop becomes a lesson in spontaneity, trying new things, and finding fun everywhere. Life’s wild moments — even spicy food fails — are what make family stories worth telling.
*Encouragement & Resilience
“When you feel like giving up, someone in our family always says, ‘You got this!’”  The food challenges push everyone past comfort zones.
Families grow stronger when they cheer each other on through challenges — big or small.
*Laughter Connects Us
“Even when we fail, we laugh it off together.” Laughter is the glue that keeps your family close — even when covered in ketchup.
*Trying New Things Builds Courage
“We never know what’s coming next… but we try it anyway!” Courage isn’t about being fearless — it’s about being willing.
*Family Traditions Create Lifelong Bonds
“Every road trip becomes a story we’ll tell forever.” Creating traditions (like goofy challenges) is how we build a legacy of joy and connection.
*Everyone Contributes Something Unique
“Every person brings something different — and that’s what makes us Ohana.”  A strong family celebrates each person’s strengths — the mix makes it magical.
*Gratitude & Appreciation for Simple Moments
“We’re so lucky to travel together and make memories — not everyone gets to do this.”  Gratitude deepens joy; adventure feels fuller when you pause to appreciate it.
*Faith & Ohana Spirit
“We call it Ohana because it means no one gets left behind — even in food battles!” Family is more than blood — it’s showing up for each other every day, in every challenge.
*Balance Fun and Realness
“It’s okay to get silly… and it’s okay to admit when you’re tired or done.”
 Real connection comes from being authentic — not perfect.

title: Goodbye? MORE big life changes!
description:
Our Daughter CONTROLS the day, before Saying GOODBYE to her before she leaves for COLLEGE...and THEN she changes her PLANS! WATCH: https://youtu.be/jG90y-3Q0Xc WATCH: https://youtu.be/m-SQMnoR64k Subscribe: https://goo.gl/dRpa1N

**IN TODAYS VIDEO: We share...
**big life changes deserve to be marked, not minimized.
Instead of treating college as “just the next step,” you pause and say:
This moment matters. You matter!
**Rykel’s “perfect day” isn’t about money or extravagance — it’s about being seen. Food she loves. Activities that reflect who she is. Conversations that matter.
** Kids feels safe enough to: Share fears, Express excitement, Deliver hard or shocking news, That doesn’t happen by accident.
**normalize the tension: Being proud AND heartbroken, Excited AND scared, 
You don’t hide the tears, and you don’t make them her responsibility either.
Healthy parenting includes emotional honesty without emotional burden on the child.
**not clinging. You’re releasing — with confidence. "Go grow. We’re still here.”
That balance is rare and incredibly reassuring to both kids and parents watching.
**honor her identity: Her preferences, Her voice, Her choices, She isn’t a storyline — she’s a person.
**shocking reveal doesn’t cause chaos — it brings conversation, closeness, and processing. Strong families don’t avoid hard conversations — they lean into them together.
**Growing Up Isn’t Leaving — It’s Expanding, College isn’t framed as abandonment.  It’s framed as expansion — for her and for the family.
**Even with change, uncertainty, and shock — the foundation stays solid.

title: is this GOODBYE? *big life change*
description:
We are LETTING You and the kids decide whether we QUIT Youtube or Continue sharing content! what's your VOTE? Celebrating 10 years was emotional! Subscribe: https://goo.gl/dRpa1N

**IN TODAYS VIDEO: We share...
1. Commitment Through Seasons
We don’t pretend YouTube was always fun or easy. We don’t quit just because something evolves or gets hard.
2. Honest Family Communication
We openly talk about: Embarrassing moments, Worst seasons, Burnout
Different opinions within the family. We have hard conversations- they belong at the table, not under the rug.
3. Everyone’s Voice Matters- The family vote is huge.
Kids aren’t just “in” the channel — they help decide its future. Parents don’t dictate; we collaborate. We Respect, autonomy, and share decision-making.
4. Growth Over Perfection- Old clips = awkward, messy, cringey. And we laugh at them instead of hiding them. Growth is something to celebrate, not erase.
5. Family vs Fame- The central question isn’t: “Is YouTube still working?”
It’s: “Is this still good for our family?” Relationships come before views, money, or algorithms.
6. Resilience & Adaptability- we show how the channel changed as: Kids got older, Interests shifted, Life seasons changed.  Families grow, and what works must grow with them.
7. Shared Ownership, Shared Responsibility- we don’t frame the channel as “mom & dad’s thing.”  It’s an Ohana thing. When we build something together, we protect it together.
8. Gratitude & Reflection- Looking back intentionally on:  Favorite moments, Lowest points, Lessons learned.  Reflection helps us move forward wisely, not reactively.

title: We SNUCK OUT 🤫 and Threw a SECRET PARTY!
description:
We Ditched School & SNUCK into the SKATING RINK & didn't plan on throwing a Party, but we did....and it all got OUT OF CONTROL! Watch this: https://youtu.be/5vGuuWA1pWs
Subscribe: https://goo.gl/dRpa1N

**IN TODAYS VIDEO: We share...
*Responsibility Comes with Freedom
The kids want to be independent and plan a “fun day” on their own — but they quickly learn that freedom isn’t just about fun, it’s about making smart choices and managing consequences.
*Honesty Builds Trust
At first, they hide their plans from Mom and Dad, thinking it’s “no big deal.”
When things spiral out of control (too many friends, chaos at the rink), they realize honesty upfront could have avoided a lot of stress.
Key takeaway: telling the truth early always turns out better than trying to cover up later.
*Teamwork Solves Problems
Once everything goes sideways, the siblings have to work together to fix it — organizing rides, cleaning up, calming things down, and eventually calling for help.
Shows how teamwork and communication can turn a messy situation into a bonding experience.
*Learning from Mistakes is Part of Growing Up
The kids make real, relatable mistakes — overconfidence, peer pressure, and trying to “do it all.”
Instead of harsh punishment, there’s a focus on learning, reflection, and growth.
Message: it’s okay to mess up, as long as you take accountability and learn something.
*Family Always Has Your Back
Even when the kids get in over their heads, they can still call their parents for help — and the parents show up.
Reinforces that family is a safety net, not a judgment zone.
Highlights love, forgiveness, and grace within strong family bonds.
*Leadership and Peer Influence
Wyatt’s role as the “leader” of the group comes into focus — his decisions affect everyone else.
Demonstrates the pressure of leadership and the importance of thinking about others before acting.
*Fun Has Boundaries
The day starts carefree and wild, but the story naturally shows how rules and boundaries actually protect the fun.
structure makes adventures more enjoyable and safe.
*Communication Matters
Miscommunication among siblings and friends adds to the chaos.
The resolution shows how checking in, listening, and being clear prevents drama.
*Gratitude for Parents
After needing parents’ help, the kids have a new appreciation for all the behind-the-scenes effort parents do (driving, organizing, supervising).
*Real Consequences, Real Growth
Maybe there’s cleanup, apology calls, or a discussion afterward.
Shows that consequences aren’t about punishment — they’re about learning to make better choices next time.

title: ALL together for CHRISTMAS! [2025 what we got]
description:
We tried to keep Christmas simple, but it didn't work, like usual.  But our Kids reactions were everything.  Watch our SECRET SANTA here: https://youtu.be/JgZfeednORA and the Sibling exchange HERE: https://youtu.be/nsuAymLI78I
Subscribe: https://goo.gl/dRpa1N

**IN TODAYS VIDEO: We share...
1. Togetherness Over Things
Christmas is something you do together, not just something you open.
Sitting together, Laughing, searching, eating, reacting. The day is about shared moments, not individual gifts.  Insight: Presence matters more than presents.
2. Joy Is Found in the Experience
The treasure hunt turns gift-giving into an experience instead of a transaction.
Insight: Memories last longer than stuff.
3. Gratitude & Appreciation. Gratitude is taught by example, not reminders.
4. Balanced Approach to Gift-Giving
showing joy in gifts without excess or pressure.Not about “who got more”
Not about comparison. Focused on meaning.  Insight: Gifts are symbols of love, not measures of worth.
5. Kids Learn What You Celebrate
By celebrating: Togetherness, Patience, Fun, Gratitude.  You teach kids what truly matters.
Insight: What parents emphasize becomes children’s values.
6. Intentional Parenting Doesn’t Have to Be Perfect
Real reactions, real chaos, real joy.  Messy moments, Imperfect timing, Authentic emotions
Insight: Kids don’t need perfect holidays — they need connected ones.
7. Creativity Over Consumption
The treasure hunt shows: Creativity beats spending, Thoughtfulness over flash, Planning over pressure.  Insight: You don’t need more money to create more joy.
8. Slowing Down Is a Gift: Christmas breakfast + unhurried moments reinforce: Rest, Presence, Enjoying the morning instead of rushing it
Insight: Slowing down is one of the greatest gifts you can give your family.

White Bean Chicken Chili Recipe
Ingredients:
2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken breasts
2 cans white northern beans, drained
1 can cream of chicken soup
2 cans of chicken broth
2 cans of corn
1 can chopped green chiles
1/2 cup of water
2 tsp ground cumin
1 tsp onion powder
1 tsp garlic powder
salt and pepper to taste
pepper jack cheese, shredded

Directions:
1. Place uncooked chicken breasts in the crockpot.
2. Add all of the remaining ingredients to your crockpot and gently mix together.
3. Cook on high for approximately 4 hours or low 6-7 hours.
4. Before serving shred the pieces of chicken into bite size pieces.
5. Serve with some crushed tortilla chips and shredded pepper jack cheese on top.

title: I Lost My Memory!
description:

We rush her to the hospital, terrified she could hurt herself if her memory doesn’t come back. Doctors say time will tell, so we take matters into our own hands.

We try everything to jog her memory:
☕ Starbucks runs
🌊 Visiting her favorite lake
📸 Replaying old memories
🧩 Showing her clues from her life

But the more we try, the more scared we get that we’re losing our sister for good.

Then we start noticing things that don’t add up.
Strange gaps.

And a feeling that this might not have been a simple fall after all…

title: Gumball Machine Sharing is Caring Lesson
description:
Nicole and Mike, two friends who really, really want to play with the same big gumball machine toy. Uh-oh! They both grab it at the same time and oh no! The toy breaks into two pieces. 😢 Nicole and Mike each take a piece, but it's just not the same. They can't play ball pit and it's not working.

But here comes Uncle to save the day! 🦸‍♂️ He has a great idea. He tells the children that if they agree to share the toy, he will fix it for them. They think about it and decide to give it a try. Yay! Uncle fixes the toy, and now Nicole and Mike can play together with the whole gumball machine. 🎉 Uncle reminds them, “Kids, sharing is caring, no more fighting, ok!!!”

Nicole and Mike learn a valuable lesson about sharing and working together. They find out that when they share, they both get to have fun, and their toys don’t get broken. Remember kids, sharing is always caring! 💖
